newsitem.title: GERMANY: EMU must be on time with criteria met - Duisenberg.
newsitem.headline: EMU must be on time with criteria met - Duisenberg.

text.p: Dutch central bank president Wim Duisenberg said on Tuesday that European monetary and economic union (EMU) would start on time without any weakening of entry criteria.
Speaking at a news conference here with German Finance Minister Theo Waigel, Duisenberg also said mid-term economic conditions should be taken into consideration for EMU.
EMU must be on time with criteria met-Duisenberg
When asked if EMU would start on time without loosening the fiscal criteria laid out in the Maastricht Treaty, Duisenberg said, "Yes."
But he added: "However, that same section of the Maastricht Treaty also takes into account the mid-term economic development of a would-be member state, looking ahead to 1998 and further."
Duisenberg is supposed to take over as head of the European Monetary Institute on July 1 and is seen as a strong candidate to be the first president of the European Central Bank.
The ECB will oversee the planned launch of the single European currency in 1999.

"As far as I know, there is only one candidate for the presidency of the European Central Bank and I know of no better candidate than Wim Duisenberg," Waigel said at the headquarters of his Christian Social (CSU) party.
